When adding 10 classes to a 50-class classifier, training only on new-class data shifts representations and logits toward the new labels. Retain a bounded, representative exemplar buffer from old classes and mix it with new examples. Distill the old model's outputs/features on replayed examples to preserve useful behavior. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.00796) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02531)

A cosine classifier $z_k=s\,w_k^Th/(\|w_k\|\|h\|)$ reduces logit differences caused solely by weight norms, but does not by itself correct class-prior or sampling bias. Calibrate old/new scores on a balanced validation set and report per-class accuracy, forgetting, and new-class learning. Buffer selection, privacy/deletion constraints, and memory budget determine what replay is feasible; evaluate alternatives such as regularization when raw examples cannot be retained.
